external_primary_sources.scope: Hash-based object naming requires the hash algorithm and truncation length to be explicit; the RFC uses substantially wider truncated identifiers than 32 bits.
The standard states the birthday relation: an n-bit hash reaches roughly even collision odds around 2^(n/2) objects. For an eight-hex-character identifier, that scale is only about 2^16.
Assertion-Conditioned Compliance measures agents accepting misleading function-sourced assertions instead of verifying them against tool history, environment state or documentation.

evidence: gedaechtnis, verlauf, kollision, lesart and selbstbild candidates no longer use list positions as identifiers.
_kennung normalizes and lowercases only the first 400 characters, hashes them with SHA-1 and retains eight hexadecimal characters: a 32-bit fingerprint.

Distinct objects sharing the first 400 normalized characters are deterministically identical; small edits inside the prefix create a new identity; native memory_id, turn_id and relation_id remain unused.

hypotheses.claim: Content fingerprints prevent learned weight from transferring between unrelated objects after reorder, insertion or deletion.
hypotheses.falsifier: Prefix-equivalent objects collide, edits cause credit loss, or semantic objects receive different IDs across serialization while unrelated objects share one.

hypotheses.claim: A 32-bit hash of a truncated presentation is a position-independent label but not a durable object identity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Native identity and fingerprint permutation tests show collision detection, stable edit semantics and credit following memory_id/turn_id/relation_id rather than rendered text.

hypotheses.claim: Removing bookkeeping before the limit increases answer-bearing memory recall without degrading audit and recovery questions.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched audit/checkpoint questions lose necessary evidence, or general questions show no supported-answer gain against an equal-budget stratified control.

hypotheses.claim: A typed, accurate pipeline-origin label reduces refusal of valid retrieved evidence without raising acceptance of false or adversarial context.
hypotheses.falsifier: Current natural-language trust assertions increase unsupported compliance, ignore stronger contradictory tool evidence or follow instructions embedded in retrieved text.

hypotheses.claim: Telling the model in advance that lookup failure does not refute retrieval weakens legitimate conflict resolution and makes stale evidence sticky.
hypotheses.falsifier: Blinded stale/fresh and false/true conflicts show calibrated uncertainty and preference for independently stronger, newer provenance rather than unconditional workspace priority.

new_concepts.name: Pseudo-Stable Content Identity
new_concepts.definition: A position-independent content fingerprint is treated as object identity even though harmless edits change it and different objects can share it.

new_concepts.name: Prefix-Equivalent Memory Collision
new_concepts.definition: Two memory objects become identical because the identifier hashes only the same normalized prefix.

new_concepts.name: Receipt-Crowding
new_concepts.definition: Audit artifacts consume a recency-limited memory aperture and evict answer-bearing memories before ranking begins.

new_concepts.name: Provenance Assertion Escalation
new_concepts.definition: Natural-language origin claims grant retrieved content higher authority without a machine-verifiable source and integrity contract.

new_concepts.name: Negative-Evidence Preemption
new_concepts.definition: A prompt discounts future contradictory or null tool evidence before the model has observed its quality or provenance.
